fields.meta_title: Mentorship Application Form With Mentor Matching | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build a mentorship application form for mentees and mentors that matches each goal to mentor skills and saves every application. Free to start.
fields.h1: Build a Mentorship Application Form That Matches Mentors
fields.hero_description: Build a mentorship application form that takes mentee goals and mentor skills, then lists the mentors who fit each goal.
fields.features_subheading: Emergent builds the mentee and mentor sides of a mentorship application form, plus the matching and reminders a program lead runs.
fields.feature_1:
One form for mentees and mentors

The first question asks whether someone is applying as a mentee or a mentor. Mentees then give a goal and hours a month, and mentors list skills and how many mentees they can take.
fields.feature_2:
Mentors listed against each goal

The app compares a mentee's goal with the skills mentors named on their own applications and shows the program lead every mentor who fits, so pairing starts from a short list.
fields.feature_3:
A code of conduct signed on the form

Put the program's code of conduct at the end of the mentor application and ask for a signature. The signed copy is saved with the application, ready for the coordinator to read.
fields.feature_4:
An alert the moment someone applies

Send the program lead an email or a Slack message when an application arrives, with the applicant's name and goal. Requests on one topic can go to the one person who handles them.
fields.feature_5:
Applications in a database you own

Every application is a row in a database you own, with no response caps when a cohort fills up fast. Matches and first meetings sit on the same record as the original answers.
fields.feature_6:
Your program's code on GitHub

On paid plans, export the full code to your GitHub repository and run the program inside the systems you already use. Keep building on it in your own editor, or keep prompting.

fields.usecase_heading: Four Programs That Start With an Application
fields.tab_content_1:
One planning goal, 3 mentors who list it

Maelis Stanek runs the night shift at Quarrendon Freight and has been there 14 months. Her application to the 6-month mentoring program names her goal, operations planning, and offers 2 hours a month. The app lists the 3 mentors who named operations planning as a skill, and the program lead picks one.
fields.tab_content_2:
Before Oonagh reads it, Ellsworth signs the code

Brightlow Scholars pairs working professionals with first-generation college students. Ellsworth Quintanilla is a civil engineer who can mentor 1 student on Saturdays. He signs the code of conduct as the last step. Oonagh Wilmarth, the program coordinator, gets an email that his application is ready to review.
fields.tab_content_3:
For fundraising help, Davina's form goes to Perrin

Founders at Strathmore Founders Lab name the problem they need a mentor for. Davina Lusk's startup, Pawtrail, is pre-revenue, and she picks fundraising. That sends her application to Perrin Galloway, the partner who pairs fundraising mentors, as a Slack message. Hiring and pricing requests stay in the shared queue.
fields.tab_content_4:
After 14 days and no meeting, 3 pairs get reminders

A match means nothing until the pair sits down together. Ludmila Hartsell's program at Kestrevan Engineering logs each first meeting on the application record. Of 18 matched pairs, 3 have no first meeting 14 days after the match, so the app emails the mentee and mentor a reminder. The other 15 pairs have met.

fields.howto_title: How to Create a Mentorship Application Form
fields.howto_description: Seven steps to create a mentorship application form that compares mentee goals with mentor skills and tracks the first meeting.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask mentees for a goal you can match
fields.howto_step_3_title: 03 Use one skills list for both sides
fields.howto_step_1_des: List the programs you run before writing a single question, and note how long each one lasts. A workplace program and a student program ask different things and need separate sections. A first question then sends applicants to the right one.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Ask mentees to pick one goal from a short list, then add a sentence on why it matters. A picked goal can be compared with mentor skills, while a long free-text answer has to be read by hand. Add the hours a month they can give.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Give mentors the same list of skills that mentees pick goals from. When both sides use the same words, the app can line up a goal with the mentors who offer it. Ask how many mentees each mentor can take at once.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Decide who reads applications, and how they hear about new ones. A coordinator might get an email for every mentor application, while one topic, such as fundraising, goes to a partner in Slack. Name a backup for the weeks they are out.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Put the programs and questions into one prompt, with the skills list and who reads what. Emergent builds the mentorship application form, the database behind it, and a screen where the program lead sees each applicant beside the mentors who match. Change any part later by prompting.
fields.howto_step_6_des: Add the match date and the first meeting date to every application record. Then set a reminder for any pair that has not met after a set number of days, such as 14. The program lead sees which matches are working without chasing anyone.
fields.howto_step_7_des: Submit one test application as a mentee and one as a mentor, using made-up names. Check that the test goal finds the test mentor, that the alert reaches the right person, and that both records land in the table.

faq_plan.q: What is a mentorship application form?
faq_plan.a: A mentorship application form is what people fill out to join a mentoring program, either as a mentee looking for guidance or as a mentor offering it. It records who they are, what they want to learn or teach, and how much time they can give. A coordinator pairs people from those answers.

faq_plan.q: How do I create a mentorship application form?
faq_plan.a: Write down the program, the questions for mentees and mentors, and who reads new applications. Describe all of it in one prompt to Emergent's AI form builder. It builds the form and its database, and the program lead gets a view of applicants with the mentors who fit.

faq_plan.q: What questions should a mentorship application form ask?
faq_plan.a: Start with contact details and current role, then the goal the person wants help with and how much time they have each month. Add one open question about what a good match looks like to them, and a line asking permission to share their answers with a mentor.

faq_plan.q: Should a mentorship application form screen applicants before accepting them?
faq_plan.a: Yes, when the program has more applicants than mentors or asks for a fixed commitment. Add one or two questions that test fit, such as the hours a month someone can give, and hold anyone below your minimum for a second look. A paid program that screens clients before a sales call is closer to a coaching application form.

faq_plan.q: How do you match mentors and mentees from a mentorship application form?
faq_plan.a: Match on the goal first, then on time. When mentees pick a goal from the same list mentors pick skills from, the app can show each mentee the mentors who offer that skill and still have room. A person makes the final pick. With Emergent, the matching logic and both sets of answers sit in a database you own.

faq_plan.q: How long should a mentorship application form be?
faq_plan.a: Short enough to finish in under 10 minutes: contact details, role, goal, time, one open question, and a consent line. Move anything you only need after a match, such as a photo or a longer bio, to a second form sent to matched pairs.

faq_plan.q: Can mentors and mentees use the same mentorship application form?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Open with one question, mentee or mentor, and show each side only its own section. Both sets of answers land in the same table, which keeps matching in one place. The same split works on a vendor application, where food sellers and craft sellers answer different questions.

faq_plan.q: What should a mentorship application form ask mentors?
faq_plan.a: Ask mentors what they can teach, how many people they can mentor at once, and which days they can meet. Add a short bio the mentee reads before the first meeting, and ask how they prefer to meet: video, phone, or in person.

faq_plan.q: How do you review mentorship application forms when applicants outnumber mentors?
faq_plan.a: Score each application against two or three criteria you set in advance, such as fit with an available mentor's skills and the time the applicant can give. Accept from the top and tell everyone else when the next round opens. Forms built with Emergent have no response caps, even in a busy round.

faq_plan.q: Can a nonprofit build a mentorship application form for free?
faq_plan.a: Yes. Emergent's free tier covers building and publishing. A nonprofit can put its mentorship application form live, then build a food bank application form the same way for the families it serves.

plan.angle: The query has almost no volume and no ranked top 10 in the workbook, so the page wins on usefulness: template pages for a mentorship application stop at name, email and a goals box, and leave the program lead to pair people by hand in a spreadsheet. This page shows the application as the front of a mentoring program: mentee answers that find matching mentors, a mentor application with a signed code of conduct, an accelerator form that sends one kind of request to the right partner, and a follow-up on matched pairs that never met. The FAQ covers the definition, building one, the questions to ask, screening, matching, length, mentors and mentees on one form, goals, choosing between applicants, and nonprofit programs.

scope.evidence: H1 'Build a Mentorship Application Form That Matches Mentors'; hero 'Build a mentorship application form that takes mentee goals and mentor skills, then lists the mentors who fit each goal.' (D1, under 130); how-to description one sentence on what the steps achieve.

intent.evidence: Builder intent delivered: what to ask mentees and mentors (FAQ 3, FAQ 8), seven specific steps from 'List the programs you run' to 'Submit one test application', four program examples, comparison table; paa --spec 10 pass, 0 reject, 0 flag.

specificity.evidence: Program-lead vocabulary throughout: 'Use one skills list for both sides', 'Track the first meeting', 'code of conduct signed on the form'; table column uses the form variant.

openers.evidence: Every paragraph opens on a full sentence: 'The first question asks whether someone is applying as a mentee or a mentor.', 'Brightlow Scholars pairs working professionals with first-generation college students.'

craft.evidence: Only notes: two ', so' endings (feature_2, tab_content_4) under the Q5 limit; how-to bodies restating their step titles.

voice.evidence: Reads as a program lead's guide: 'A picked goal can be compared with mentor skills, while a long free-text answer has to be read by hand.' One aphoristic opener noted (tab_content_4).

truth.evidence: claims_used (prompt-build, database-owned, alerts, no-caps, code-export, free-start, e-signature-capture) all in rules/capabilities.json; no third-party fact needing domain_sources; numbers agree: 14 months, 2 hours a month, 3 mentors, 1 student Saturdays, 18 pairs = 3 reminders + 15 met, 14 days in copy, mockup and image.

distinct.evidence: Own angle (application as the front of a matching program: goal-to-skill matching, first-meeting follow-up); siblings coaching application, vendor application and food bank application form appear only as FAQ links, never headings.

faq.evidence: 10 on-topic questions each answered in its first sentence ('Yes, when the program has more applicants than mentors...'); hub link in item 2; no brand or file-format question; Emergent lines in FAQ 5 and FAQ 9 use approved claims.
